title: Masafee CTF 7B: QLoRA Fine-Tuning of a 7B Code Model on CTF Writeups for Stylistic and Knowledge Adaptation
description:
Empirical study of QLoRA continued pretraining of a 7B code model (Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B Instruct) on 18,013 CTF (Capture-the-Flag) writeup chunks scraped from CTFtime.org. The fine-tuned model is evaluated on the CyberMetric-500 cybersecurity knowledge benchmark and a 30-challenge subset of the NYU CTF Bench alongside the base model and Cisco's Foundation-Sec-8B-Instruct.

Key findings: (1) continued pretraining on writeup text produces measurable style transfer (directness, CTF-specific terminology) but no measurable capability gain on knowledge MCQs or single-shot CTF problem solving; (2) style overfitting can actively impede flag-answer extraction; (3) the writeup-trained model exhibits an 11x lower hedging-language rate than the SOC-tuned Foundation-Sec-8B, reflecting domain-specific training-data priors rather than a quality difference.

All training was performed on a single consumer GPU (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 12GB) in 12 hours 17 minutes (~150 JPY in electricity). The companion LoRA adapter and Q4_K_M GGUF weights are distributed on Hugging Face under a research-and-personal-use-only license (derivative of CTFtime writeups whose copyright belongs to individual contributors). The code, scripts, evaluation report, and documentation in this repository are released under the MIT license.
